work_item.role: W1 public-evidence discovery and neutral admission

discovery_pass.method: Direction-blind admission of a pinned public cross-agent result table from Hackathon-24h. The result snapshot identifies three native CLI harnesses, one publisher-declared underlying Kimi-K2.5 model, the same HTTP Server 47-test-point benchmark, and the same 24-hour window. No raw per-run trajectories/logs are committed, so the observations are preserved explicitly as weaker published-table evidence with material execution details left unknown.

source_known_dimensions: publisher explicitly states the same underlying Kimi-K2.5 model across the three harness frameworks
same Hackathon-24h HTTP Server benchmark with 47 published test points
same benchmark snapshot and public HTTP evaluator implementation
same dual-loop architecture: Docker-isolated agent loop plus host-side periodic benchmark loop with anonymized feedback
same project-scale HTTP Server objective and source-listed h1spec/CISPA/TechEmpower evaluation families
explicit_unknown_or_nonidentical_dimensi: exact Claude Code/OpenCode/Cline package revisions because the pinned Docker recipe installs @latest
exact historical provider/base-URL/auth route per harness run
exact experiment dates, host hardware, and built container image digests
raw per-run logs and trajectories are not committed
session reset, compaction, retry and adaptation details are not reconstructable per harness
iteration counts differ as observed outcomes
publisher's identical-conditions statement cannot be independently verified against missing raw run artifacts

provenance_strength.w1_treatment: admitted as weaker pinned-table evidence; absence of raw run artifacts remains an explicit limitation and does not become inferred comparability

non_admission_dispositions.reason: Pass 14 conservatively did not admit the table because no committed raw per-run artifact was located. That append-only historical disposition is not edited. Under the current PUBLIC-EVIDENCE contract, pinned public benchmark result tables are admissible when concrete system/result identity is supportable, so pass 19 admits the same published table with public_logs/public_trajectories/raw_run_artifacts explicitly false.

non_admission_dispositions.surface: publisher claim that harness differences caused the score spread
non_admission_dispositions.reason: W1 records only the published scores, benchmark identity, source-declared same model and known/unknown execution dimensions; causal interpretation is downstream.
W1 does not declare a winner or interpret score direction.

commands_required: python scripts/admission_check.py <each of three pass-19 raw records>

results.scope: temporary write-enabled registry regeneration plus repository validation and three record-specific admission checks
